description:
Two fixtures carry wall-clock timeout overrides that were deliberately tightened
to act as perf tripwires: `enum_predicate_search` (was 6s against a ~3.15s local
compile) and `enum_take_drop_split` (15s against 6.1s). The idea was sound -- a
tiny program that compiles for seconds is doing excess work, and that is a
correctness signal, not a perf nit -- but wall-clock is the wrong instrument.

## Why the tripwire failed

A budget calibrated on dev hardware cannot gate CI. The runners are much slower
and run under `llvm-cov` instrumentation. `enum_predicate_search::run` and
`::interp` exceeded their cap on EVERY CI run of the fz-go4.1..fz-f98.19 branch
stack -- PRs #80, #90, #91, #92 and #99 -- and nobody noticed, because from #93
to #98 the lib suite failed first and cargo's fail-fast meant the matrix never
ran at all. The failure only became visible when fz-f98.19 made the lib suite
green. A tripwire that is always red teaches everyone to ignore it, which is
strictly worse than having none.

The caps are now loose hang backstops (15s), documented as such in the fixture
headers, and deliberately too coarse to notice a perf regression.

## What replaces it

A work-based assertion, which is machine independent and names the defect when
it fires. [[feedback_minimal_job_trace_acceptance]] already describes the shape:
gate on the `--log-telemetry` job trace being minimal versus expected work.

fz-xat already measured the number for this exact fixture: 2625
`callable_construction` settlements for 242 executables. That is the assertion
-- a settlement/derivation count ceiling per fixture -- not a duration.

## Design notes

- The count must come from telemetry the compiler already emits, not a
  test-only counter ([[feedback_tests_use_production_paths]]). `DemandConeSettlement`
  (members / external_members / rounds / derivations) exists and is emitted;
  check whether it is sufficient before adding anything.
- A ceiling, not an equality: it should fail on a REGRESSION, and quietly
  tighten as fz-xat lands improvements.
- It belongs where the fixture metadata already lives, so it is declared in the
  fixture header next to `timeout.*` rather than in a side table.
- Only fixtures with a known excess-work story need one. Do not add a ceiling to
  every fixture.

## Checks

- `enum_predicate_search` carries a work ceiling that fails if settlement volume
  regresses, and passes at HEAD.
- The ceiling is derived from emitted telemetry, with no test-only counting.
- The wall-clock overrides stay loose and stay documented as hang backstops.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.

## Related

- fz-xat is the actual excess work (2625 settlements for 242 executables); this
  ticket is only the detector that keeps it from regressing further.
- fz-1iw retires timeout overrides that are no longer needed at all; this is the
  opposite case, where the override stays but stops pretending to be a gate.
title: Replace the wall-clock perf tripwire with a work-count ceiling from telemetry
